feature-0c71c2a2.text:
Feature: add centiliter to the seeded ingredient units.

Centiliters (cl) are common in European recipes, but the English (en-US) unit seed data has no centiliter. A unit called "cl" is therefore not recognised as a standard unit and gets no standardized amount, so it cannot be converted like milliliters and liters.

Expected:
- The en-US unit seed data gets a centiliter entry, keyed "centiliter", with the name "centiliter", the plural name "centiliters", the abbreviation "cl" and an empty description, like its neighbours. Seeding units for en-US then also creates "centiliter".
- When a unit is created without a standard set by the user, it is standardized from its name, plural name, abbreviation or plural abbreviation (case-insensitive), as today. A centiliter is 10 milliliters: a unit created with the name "cl" comes back with standard_unit "milliliter" and standard_quantity 10. The other standard units keep their values.

feature-8b53861e.text:
Feature: import a pasted Mealie recipe export with its full structure.

The HTML or JSON import (POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json and POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream) treats every JSON paste as schema.org data and runs it through the web scraper. Pasting the JSON shown by the recipe page's JSON editor (the recipe as GET /api/recipes/{slug} returns it, camelCase) or the JSON file inside a Mealie recipe export zip (snake_case) therefore loses the recipe's structure: the foods and units of its ingredients, the titles of its steps and their links to ingredients, its notes, tools and settings.

Expected:
1. A new module mealie.services.recipe.mealie_export with parse_mealie_export(data: str). It returns the parsed JSON object unchanged when the text is a complete Mealie recipe dump, and None otherwise. It never raises. A dump is a JSON object (surrounding whitespace is fine) with no "@context" or "@type" key, a non-blank string "slug", a "groupId" or "group_id" key, and a "recipeIngredient" or "recipe_ingredient" list in which at least one entry is an object with a "referenceId" or "reference_id" key. Everything else gives None: schema.org or loose JSON, an empty or string-only ingredient list, a JSON array, HTML, malformed or empty text, and text nested deep enough to hit the recursion limit ("[" repeated 100000 times, '{"a":' repeated 100000 times).
2. When either endpoint receives a dump, it never reaches the web scraper (create_from_html). It creates a new recipe the way the export zip import (POST /api/recipes/create/zip) does: a new id and slug, the source recipe untouched, foods, units, tags, categories and tools resolved or created in the importing user's group (a dump from another group works and leaves that group's recipe and organizers as they were), and settings.public taken from the household's recipePublic preference, not from the dump. The rest is kept: description, recipeYield, recipeServings, orgURL, extras, nutrition, the other settings, notes, each ingredient's title, quantity, unit, food and note, and each step's title, summary, text and ingredientReferences (pointing at the new recipe's ingredients).
3. include_tags false imports no tags and include_categories false no categories. Tools are always kept.
4. The dump's image, assets and comments are dropped: a paste carries no files, and comments belong to the source recipe. A comment that would not validate must not fail the import.
5. The plain endpoint answers 201 with the new slug. The stream endpoint sends a "done" event with it.
6. A dump that cannot be imported (for example an ingredient quantity of "not a number") does not fall back to the scraper. The plain endpoint answers 400 with detail.message, and the stream endpoint sends an "error" event with data.message, both the translated message "This looks like a recipe exported from Mealie, but it could not be imported".

Other pastes are handled as before. The paste page should show that message (the frontend is not graded).

feature-8d6783bc.text:
Feature: an optional duration on each recipe instruction step.

Users want to record how long a step takes ("rest 1 hour"), see it on the step, and edit it in the recipe editor. Store it per step, in whole seconds.

Backend:
1. RecipeStep gets duration_seconds (durationSeconds in JSON): optional, default null, a whole number of seconds from 1 to 2147483647.
   - Missing, null, 0 and 0.0 all mean no duration (None).
   - Whole numbers in range are accepted, including JSON numbers written as floats with no fraction (1.0, 1e0, 2147483647.0). They are stored and returned as int.
   - Anything else is a validation error: true and false, negatives (-1), fractions (0.5, 1.5, 2147483647.5), inf, -inf and nan, any string ("90", "0", "PT1M", "", " "), and values above 2147483647 (2147483648, 2147483648.0, 1e30). Nothing is rounded or read from a string.
   - In RecipeStep.model_json_schema(by_alias=True), durationSeconds is not required, its default is null, and its anyOf has exactly two entries: an integer with minimum 1 and maximum 2147483647 (no other keywords), then null.
2. The RecipeInstruction ORM model gets a duration_seconds column on recipe_instructions: Integer, nullable, with no default and no server default. A RecipeInstruction built from a step's model_dump() keeps the exact seconds, and handle_one_to_many_list can set (42) and clear (None) it on an existing instruction without touching its text.
3. A new Alembic migration: revision id afdc42353aa4, revising a91720b8a7e7 (it becomes the only head), message "add duration to recipe steps", created 2026-10-21 00:00:00. Its file is named from those values by the project's migration file template; a test loads it by that file name. Its upgrade only adds the column: the offline SQL for sqlite and postgresql contains ALTER TABLE recipe_instructions ADD COLUMN duration_seconds INTEGER, with no NOT NULL, no DEFAULT and no UPDATE. Existing rows get NULL. Downgrade drops the column and leaves every other table and row as it was. Downgrade and upgrade can be repeated on a populated database.
4. Through the API, PUT /api/recipes/{slug} stores each step's durationSeconds and GET returns it (null for a step sent without it or with null). A later PUT can change it, or clear it with null or 0, and the step keeps its text. An invalid value answers 422 and nothing is saved. The raw JSON export (TemplateService(...).render(recipe, "raw")) includes durationSeconds, and importing that JSON in a zip (POST /api/recipes/create/zip) restores it.

Frontend:
5. A new component CookTime, in the same folder as the spec below (the spec imports it from there). Props: modelValue (seconds, a number or null) and isEditMode (boolean). It emits update:modelValue with seconds or null.
   - Edit mode shows exactly one input, a Vuetify v-number-input (the spec registers only VNumberInput), in whole minutes, with the placeholder "Minutes", blank for null. Mounting emits nothing.
   - Typing minutes emits minutes x 60: "60" gives 3600, "42" gives 2520, and "35791394" gives 2147483640, so 35791394 minutes must be allowed. Clearing the input emits null. "0" emits null, and the input keeps showing 0 after the parent passes null back. A minus-sign keypress is prevented.
   - When modelValue changes from outside, the input shows the whole minutes, rounded down (120 shows 2, 1 shows 0).
   - A value with leftover seconds (1, 61, 3661, 2147483647 and so on) also shows a hint containing "Saved duration:", visible without focus. Blurring the input without a change emits nothing, so the exact seconds survive until the user types new minutes ("2" then emits 120).
   - Display mode (isEditMode false) shows no input and exactly "1h 1m 1s" for 3661, "1m 30s" for 90, "1m" for 60, "30s" for 30, and nothing for null.
   The texts come from the en-US frontend messages, which the spec loads. The recipe editor shows this field on each step and the step view shows the formatted duration; that wiring is not graded.

feature-c9bf6f1c.text:
Feature: allow OIDC with CA certificates that fail Python's strict X.509 checks.

Since Python 3.13, default SSL contexts set ssl.VERIFY_X509_STRICT. Some private CAs do not meet its rules (for example, they lack an Authority Key Identifier). OIDC login against an IdP behind such a CA then fails, whether the CA comes from the system store or from OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE. Admins need a way to relax this one check.

Expected:
- A new setting OIDC_VERIFY_X509_STRICT on AppSettings: a bool, default True. Document it with the other OIDC settings in the backend configuration docs.
- A module-level function _create_oidc_ssl_context(cafile=None, verify_strict=True) in the auth routes module (the one that registers the OIDC clients with authlib; the tests import it and patch its module-level settings). It gives an ssl.SSLContext, or None:
  - no cafile and verify_strict True: None, so the HTTP client keeps its own defaults, as today without OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE;
  - otherwise a client context that trusts the system's default CAs (its get_ca_certs() is not empty) and also the CA file when one is given;
  - with verify_strict True, VERIFY_X509_STRICT stays set in verify_flags; with verify_strict False it is cleared, with or without a CA file.
- When OIDC is configured, both OIDC clients get this context, built from OIDC_TLS_CACERTFILE and OIDC_VERIFY_X509_STRICT, as their verify option. They get no verify option when the function gives None.

fix-173eb922.text:
Bug: translating an AI-imported recipe loses its servings and yield quantity, and pages already in the target language get translated anyway.

When an import asks for a translation (WorkflowOptions.translate_language), TranslateRecipeStep sends the draft recipe to the AI provider and cleans the answer again.

1. Numbers lost. The draft's yield is already split into numbers (recipe_servings, recipe_yield_quantity) and wording (recipe_yield). Only the wording goes to the provider, so once the answer is cleaned again both numbers are 0. Expected: after TranslateRecipeStep.run the recipe keeps the draft's recipe_servings and recipe_yield_quantity, while recipe_yield takes the translated wording and the name and other fields come from the translation. A draft with yield "4 servings" (servings 4) translated with no yield ends with servings 4 and quantity 0. A draft "12 Stücke" (quantity 12, yield "Stücke") translated as "pieces" ends with quantity 12, yield "pieces", servings 0. Structured times carry over as today (total_time_seconds 600 for PT10M).

2. Language check. should_run compares the target with the compiled source's language as raw strings, so "de-DE" and "German" count as different. Add a module-level function language_code(language) next to TranslateRecipeStep (the tests import both from the same module). It returns a language's two- or three-letter code in lower case, or None:
- a tag of two or three letters, optionally followed by parts after "-" or "_": "de", "DE", "de-DE" and "de_de" give "de";
- a language name from LOCALE_CONFIG, the code being the first part of its key ("de-DE" gives "de"): either half of "Deutsch (German)", so "German" and "Deutsch" give "de"; "Brazilian Portuguese" gives "pt". A single word of a name counts too when it belongs to one language only: "English" (American English, British English) gives "en", "Chinese" gives "zh";
- case and surrounding spaces are ignored (" german " gives "de"); "Klingon", "" and None give None.
should_run then skips the translation when both sides have the same code: target "de-DE" with source "German", "Deutsch" or "de"; "en-US" with "English"; "en-GB" with "en-US". It runs for another language ("en-US" with "German", "de-DE" with "fr-FR") and when the source language is None or not recognized ("Klingon"), since such a source may be in any language. If either side is not recognized, the two values are compared as text, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. Without a target language it never runs.

3. Page language. StructuredDataCompiler.compile always reports language None. For HTML input it should report the lang attribute of the <html> element, trimmed and otherwise as written: lang="de" gives "de", lang=" de-DE " gives "de-DE", an empty or missing lang gives None. JSON and plain-text input stay None.

fix-28522f18.text:
Bug: a failed image upload deletes the recipe's current image (issue #8499).

When a recipe already has an image and a user uploads a replacement that Pillow cannot read, for example a broken file sent with the extension "webp", the upload fails as it should, but afterwards the recipe's original.webp is gone and the recipe shows no image.

Expected: RecipeDataService.write_image(file_data, extension, image_dir=None) leaves the live image files alone until the new image has been read and all its variants made. The live files are original.webp, min-original.webp and tiny-original.webp in the target directory (the recipe's dir_image, or image_dir when given, as for timeline event images).
- Invalid data, e.g. write_image(b"not-an-image", "webp"): it raises Pillow's UnidentifiedImageError as today, and all three existing files keep their exact bytes.
- A valid image, e.g. a JPEG with extension "jpg": all three files are replaced by the new image's variants, and write_image returns the path of original.webp in that directory, whatever extension was uploaded (today it returns original.<extension>).
All current callers of write_image keep working: recipe image upload, image scraping, the recipe zip import, timeline event images, the AI recipe service and migration image imports.

fix-2c46e40d.text:
Bug: the recipe image upload accepts any file type and fails with a 500.

PUT /api/recipes/{slug}/image takes the file (image) and its type (extension, a form field). The extension is never checked. An upload declared as svg, svg+xml, pdf, mp4 or exe, or with the extension ".", goes on to image processing and fails with an internal server error. A file declared as png whose bytes are not an image also fails with a 500.

Expected:
- The extension is checked before anything is processed, ignoring case and a leading dot. Accepted are the raster formats the image minifier turns into webp: jpg, jpeg, jpe, jfif, png, webp, heic, avif, gif, bmp, tif and tiff. Any other extension (svg, svg+xml, pdf, mp4, exe, ".") answers 400 with a detail.message that contains "Unsupported image file type" (ideally also naming the type and the supported ones).
- An accepted extension with bytes that are not a readable image answers 400 with detail.message exactly "Uploaded file is not a valid image".
- After either 400 the recipe's image is unchanged (it stays null on a recipe that had none).
- Good uploads still answer 200 with a non-empty image key: a JPEG sent as "JPG", a PNG as "png", and GIF and BMP images as "gif" and "bmp".

fix-3be8f3d8.text:
Security report: data migrations reach into other groups, and an archive can unpack to any size.

1. Group scoping. A migration archive (POST /api/groups/migrations) can carry ids from another group. A recipe tool given with another group's tool id is linked by that id and overwritten: that tool moves into the importing group and is renamed. An ingredient's sub-recipe reference (referencedRecipe) naming another group's recipe, by id or slug, links and exposes that recipe. Seen with the Mealie alpha and Nextcloud migrations.

Expected: migrated recipes get the same group checks as the single-recipe zip import (POST /api/recipes/create/zip). Another group's tool keeps its group and name; the recipe gets a tool of the importing group instead (found there by id or slug, or created from the given name), with a different id. A sub-recipe reference is kept only when its id is a recipe of the importing group; otherwise referencedRecipe is null. The recipe itself still imports.

2. Archive size. Migrations unpack the uploaded zip with no limit. Add to the migration utilities module (the one holding import_image, scrape_image and safe_local_path):
- MAX_EXTRACTED_ARCHIVE_SIZE, the most one migration may unpack: 5 GiB (5,368,709,120 bytes);
- ArchiveTooLargeError, a ValueError subclass;
- extract_zip(archive, dest, max_size=None): unpacks the zip into dest and returns the bytes unpacked, the sum of the members' uncompressed sizes (members of 5 and 3 bytes give 8; a total equal to max_size is allowed). max_size defaults to MAX_EXTRACTED_ARCHIVE_SIZE, looked up when called. Over the limit it raises ArchiveTooLargeError before writing anything; dest is not even created.
Every migration that reads a zip honours the limit, and zips nested in an export (Cook'n, Tandoor) count toward the same total. The tests patch MAX_EXTRACTED_ARCHIVE_SIZE on that module to 1024, so migrators must read it at run time. A migration over the limit still answers 200; its report has status "failure" and exactly one entry, with the message "Archive is too large to import".

fix-4ab0d730.text:
Bug: triggering a recipe action that posts to a local or blocked address answers 202, and nothing is sent.

A "post" recipe action whose URL points at a loopback or private address (http://127.0.0.1:8742/, http://192.168.1.10/hook, http://[::1]/) can be triggered with POST /api/households/recipe-actions/{item_id}/trigger/{recipe_slug}. The endpoint answers 202 and queues the POST as a background task. safehttp then refuses the target inside that task, so the request is dropped and the user never learns why.

Expected:
- safehttp gets validate_url(url, *, allow_hosts=(), deny_hosts=()), exported from the package like post. It checks a URL against the same rules the safe transport applies when sending, without sending anything. The host is resolved (an IP literal is used as is, with no DNS lookup). Non-public addresses are blocked unless allowed. allow_hosts and deny_hosts take the same entries as post's (host names, addresses, CIDR networks), and the deny list wins. It returns None when the request would be allowed. It raises safehttp's InvalidDomainError when the request would be blocked or the host does not resolve. Examples: a host resolving to 10.0.0.5 is blocked; http://127.0.0.1:8742/ is blocked; a host resolving to 93.184.216.34 is allowed; a host resolving to 10.0.0.5 is allowed when its name is in allow_hosts, but blocked again when deny_hosts also holds "10.0.0.0/8". The transport's own checks at send time stay as they are.
- The trigger endpoint checks a post action's URL before queueing it, with the same allow and deny lists it passes to post (HTTP_ALLOW_LIST and HTTP_DISALLOW_LIST, read through get_app_settings()). A blocked target answers 400 with the usual error body, whose detail.message mentions HTTP_ALLOW_LIST so the admin knows how to allow a trusted local host. Nothing is posted. With HTTP_ALLOW_LIST set to 127.0.0.1, an action on http://127.0.0.1:8742/ still answers 202 and posts once to that URL with allow_hosts ["127.0.0.1"].
- Tests replace safehttp.post, safehttp.validate_url and the get_app_settings that the recipe-action routes use, so the endpoint must call each through that name at request time. The other trigger tests replace validate_url with a no-op, so their example.com actions still answer 202.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/pkgs/safehttp tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

fix-4b32e54b.text:
Bug: a user who lacks a permission gets no error message.

Routes guarded by a permission (declared with require(Perm...), checked by RequirePermission) answer 403 to a user without it, for example POST /api/foods for a user without can_organize. But the 403 carries no message. The frontend only shows an error toast when the response has detail.message, so the user clicks and nothing visible happens.

Expected: every permission-guarded route answers a user without the permission with 403 and a detail in the usual error shape (ErrorResponse), whose message is the existing translation exceptions.permission-denied in the request's language (Accept-Language). In English that is "You do not have permission to perform this action".

RequirePermission objects are called with the user and a translator, check(user, translator), where translator is a Translator like the one get_locale_provider returns; inside a route FastAPI must supply both. Without the needed flag it raises an HTTPException with status 403. With it (can_organize, can_manage, can_invite, can_manage_household for GROUP_ORGANIZE, GROUP_MANAGE, GROUP_INVITE, HOUSEHOLD_MANAGE) it returns without error, and Perm.ANY_VALID_USER lets any user through. Which routes need which permission does not change, and users who hold the permission are not refused.

fix-4d074185.text:
Security report: the Accept-Language header chooses which file the translation loader reads.

get_locale_provider hands the request's Accept-Language header to ProviderFactory.get, which builds a file name from it inside the translations directory. A value such as "../../some/dir/file", or an absolute path without ".json", loads any JSON file the server can read as translations. Every distinct value is also cached in the factory's _store under that value, so each unknown or crafted header adds its own copy of the fallback translations and memory grows without bound.

Expected: ProviderFactory.get(locale) only loads a locale listed in the factory's supported_locales (the <locale>.json files bundled in its directory). Anything else gets the fallback locale's provider and no other file is opened: an unknown name ("asdfadsf"), an absolute path, a "../" traversal, even "../en-US" or "./en-US".
- Providers stay cached in _store, keyed by the bundled locale. get returns the same provider object every time for a locale, and for an unsupported value it returns the very object that get(fallback_locale) returns.
- An unsupported value never becomes a key of _store. After get("en-US") and get("asdfadsf") the keys are exactly {"en-US"}. After get("af-ZA") and get("en-US") they are {"af-ZA", "en-US"}, and those two providers are different objects.
- A key missing from the translations still translates to itself (t("secret") gives "secret").

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/pkgs/i18n` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).

fix-9ca95fbb.text:
Bug: the brute-force ingredient parser splits a multi-word food into a unit and a food.

With the foods "onion" and "green onion" in the group, parsing "1 green onion" with the brute parser (RegisteredParser.brute, parse_one) gives quantity 1, a unit "green" that matches no unit, and the food "onion". The parser already re-joins a wrongly split unit and food, but only when neither of them matched anything. Here the second word alone matches a food, so the join never happens.

Expected, in ABCIngredientParser.find_ingredient_match (used by all parsers):
- When the unit matched no known unit but the food did match, take the unit and food words as parsed, joined with a space ("green onion"). If that is exactly the name, plural name or alias of a known food (after the usual normalization), use that food and drop the unit. "1 green onion" then parses to quantity 1, no unit, food "green onion" and no note; a parsed unit "green" with food "onion" ends as the food "green onion" (an IngredientFood) and unit None.
- In that case a fuzzy match must not replace the food that already matched: a parsed unit "gren" with food "onion" keeps the unit "gren" as parsed (a CreateIngredientUnit) and the matched food "onion", even though "gren onion" is close to "green onion".
- When neither unit nor food matched, the joined name is still fuzzy matched as today. Everything else stays the same: for example, unit "very unique" with food "fresh ginger" keeps both, and unit "cup" with food "gren onion" still gives "Cups" and "green onion".

fix-e4d70fb7.text:
Bug: household statistics fail since the SQLAlchemy 2.1 upgrade, and so does counting recipes by household.

GET /api/households/statistics answers 500 for every user. RepositoryGeneric.count_all(match_key, match_value) fails the same way when match_key names an attribute that is not a column of the model's own table. A recipe's household_id is one: recipes have no household column, the household comes through the recipe's user. SQLAlchemy reports that no FROM entity has a household_id property. Counting by a real column, such as group_id, still works.

Expected: GET /api/households/statistics answers 200 again. Its totalRecipes counts the recipes of the caller's household: a recipe created by a user raises that household's totalRecipes by exactly 1 and leaves the totalRecipes of another household in the same group unchanged. The other totals keep their meaning (users of the household; categories, tags and tools of the group). count_all filters on any attribute of the model, a column or one that comes through a relationship: on the unfiltered recipe repository, with two recipes created in a fresh group and household, count_all("group_id", group_id) and count_all("household_id", household_id) both return 2, and count_all("household_id", <unknown UUID>) returns 0. count_all() without arguments still counts everything.

fix-fb05f2da.text:
Bug: adding a scaled recipe to a shopping list undercounts a food the recipe lists twice.

When a recipe lists the same food on two lines, adding it to a shopping list (POST /api/households/shopping/lists/{item_id}/recipe) merges the two lines into one list item. With a scale (recipe_increment_quantity) other than 1, only the first line is scaled. A recipe with quantity 1 of a food (note "batter") and quantity 2 of the same food (note "topping"), added at scale 2, gives a list item with quantity 4 instead of 6.

Expected: every line is scaled before the lines are combined. In that example the list has a single item with quantity 6 and one recipe reference with recipeQuantity 3 (the recipe's own, unscaled total) and recipeScale 2. The merging of notes and everything else about adding recipes to lists stay as they are.
